authoredFrom: Input: normal-delivery.json with 194 identical truck re-sends inserted at 250 ms (one configuration step, repeat 194), so its events are 1 truck (10), 2 trailer.0 (20), 3 job (30), 4 simulation.started (40), 5-198 truck re-sends (250), 199 job re-send with cargo loaded (300), 200 simulation.paused (400), 201 simulation.started (500), 202 job.delivered (600) and 203 job cleared (610); snapshots at 100 and 200 (odometer 1,000,500 m). Its transport is a first durable connection at 0 whose client does not wait for ACKs, a disconnect at 450, a second durable connection at 460 and a disconnect at 1100. At most 203 entries are retained, below the producer's 256 (docs/native-transport-v1.md, I2).

One service with the production bound (512, ET-015c G11). The commit of eventSeq 1 is held inside its transaction while the first connection carries 1-200, so all 200 items are still queued or in flight when it ends. The second connection's checkpoint reports A = 0 and the producer redelivers 1-200 (I6). The commit is released only after the redelivered 200 reached the ingestion: 400 items are then pending, more than the old bound of 256 and inside 512, so no BACKLOG_FULL and no V1_DURABLE_RETRY (E5).

The first connection's items commit after the release without an ACK (E8) and are stepped as in normal-delivery: trip@3 opens partial with opened-at-load (T12), with truck 1 and trailer 2; the identical truck re-sends 5-198 change no reference (docs/trips.md, Identity); the road stop 100 -> 200 is a continuous 0 m step, so observed distance 0 m is persisted at the next carrier (eventSeq 5, T16).

The second welcome's session open steps the disconnection (R6): the not-connected interval runs from the last item of the first connection (eventSeq 200: label 1,800,000,000,400, source time 1,000,400,000,000 ns) to the second welcome's capture (atMs 460: 1,000,460,000,000 ns) on the capture clock. The trip is already partial, so there is no trip.update. The snapshot at 200 and the second checkpoint report odometer 1,000,500 m for the same truck, so odometerDeltaM is 0 (T16).

The redelivered 1-200 are at or below the processed point, so they are duplicates without effects (T5). The live simulation.started (201) carries the queued interval; job.delivered (202) attributes to the trip and closes it {delivered, outcome, partial} at 1,800,000,000,600 (T13, T14); the clear (203) adds nothing. 203 first commits (1-200 for the first connection, 201-203 live) and 200 duplicates.
